newsitem.title: UK: London gold drifts lower in early trading.
newsitem.headline: London gold drifts lower in early trading.

text.p: Gold was on the defensive early on Monday after slight overnight gains disappeared amid brisk selling, dealers said.
"The market is pretty quiet, but gold is seeing some decent selling this morning," said one dealer, who attributed the sales in part to gold producers.
Gold fixed at $379.70 an ounce, compared to $379.25 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $379.50/$380.00.
Prices had edged up slightly late on Friday in New York and on Far Eastern physical buying overnight. But the small gains were shortlived.
"It wasn't able to hold $380.50 in the Far East," said one dealer, referring to the highs overnight.

Gold's trading range was expected to be tight in the near term after last week's failed rally, dealers said. Prices had tumbled sharply on Friday after selling by gold producers thwarted the rally at key resistance above $384 an ounce.
"We're in a see-saw situation, with $380 as the axis," another dealer said. "Gold is going to struggle on the upside, but support from $379 on down looks good."
Dealers and technical analysts who study historical price charts said they expected gold to hold above recent lows around $377 an ounce.
"I believe it will hold. But if it breaks down, gold is in trouble," a dealer noted.
A breach of support would target fresh 19-month lows around $375 and then $372, analysts said.
Silver had helped drag gold up late on Friday in New York when it popped up to a high of $4.97 an ounce.
"I think some traders went short of silver on the back of gold, but there wasn't any real selling pressure there so that led to shortcovering," a dealer said.
But it also drifted lower and was indicated at $4.91/$4.93 an ounce, still up seven cents from Friday's London close.
Silver's prospects for further upside movement were limited, dealers said.
It order to look constructive it needed to surmount the stiff psychological resistance level of $5.00 an ounce, which has eluded the market for four weeks.
Platinum and palladium were quiet and eyeing gold for further direction.
Platinum was indicated $0.75 firmer at $384.75/$385.75 while palladium was $0.50 firmer at $118.50/$119.50.
